bib.title: SelfCheck: Using LLMs to Zero-Shot Check Their Own Step-by-Step Reasoning
bib.venue: preprint (arXiv:2308.00436v3 [cs.AI], 5 Oct 2023; no conference name printed on the PDF)

question: Can an LLM recognise errors in its own step-by-step reasoning zero-shot, without exemplars, training or external resources, and can that improve final-answer accuracy?
hypothesis: Decomposing step checking into target extraction, information collection, regeneration and comparison, which exploits generation over checking and decorrelates errors, will beat direct checking.
contributions: SelfCheck: a zero-shot step-by-step checker using a regenerate-and-compare scheme
Confidence-weighted voting over multiple solutions that raises final accuracy over majority voting on GSM8K, MathQA and MATH
Ablations of global vs step, single vs multi-stage, error-check vs regenerate-and-compare

method.summary: For each step of a CoT solution, four separate LLM calls extract the step target, select the relevant earlier information, regenerate the step from that, and compare regeneration with the original (support/contradict/not related). Step results (+1/0/-1) are combined into a confidence w in [0,1] by a sigmoid formula, used as the vote weight over several sampled solutions.
method.task: math word problem solving with step-level self-verification and weighted voting

datasets.name: MathQA
datasets.split: whole test set; 5 answer options per problem

datasets.name: MATH*
datasets.size: subset of the 5000-problem MATH test set; subset size not stated
datasets.split: subset taken from Ling et al. (2023) (MATH_np.json)
datasets.source: Hendrycks et al. 2021; subset from github.com/lz1oceani/verify_cot

other.use: generator and checker; also GPT-4 generator with GPT-3.5 checker

inference.samples: 2 solutions per question in Table 1; 1 to 10 in Fig 2 (GPT-3.5); up to 50 in Fig 5 (MathQA 100-question subset); GPT-4 runs use 2 instead of 10. Number of runs or seeds not stated.
inference.prompting: Zero-shot; same prompts for all datasets and both LLMs, with each stage a separate independent LLM call. Generator prompt asks for 'Step :' blocks separated by blank lines and ends with 'So the answer is ...'.

parameters.integration: w = 2*Sigmoid(-lambda_-1 * #(r=-1) - lambda_0 * #(r=0)); successful checks not counted
parameters.step_score: +1 support, 0 not related, -1 contradict; regex on last line for 'support'/'contradict'
parameters.classification_threshold: t, solution is correct if w >= t (varied in Fig 3/4)

other.optional_stage: variable definition extraction (Appendix A) feeds variable definitions to regeneration
other.information_ids: extracted from free-text LLM output by regular expression

metrics.name: final answer accuracy
metrics.definition: accuracy of the answer chosen by weighted vote (SelfCheck) or majority vote

metrics.name: DeltaAcc
metrics.definition: SelfCheck accuracy minus majority-voting accuracy with standard error

metrics.name: verification accuracy
metrics.definition: average of true positive and true negative rates for classifying a single solution as correct

baselines: Deductive Verification and Self-Verification, quoted from earlier work, not directly comparable (need exemplars)
Ablation variants: global check, single-stage check, error check 0-shot and 1-shot
eval.protocol: Standard errors on accuracy differences; no significance test named. Faithful-CoT omitted since Ling et al. found it lowers accuracy; finetuned verifiers not compared.

prompts.text: The following is a part of the solution to the problem [Question]: [Step 0,..., Step i]. What specific action does the step [Step i] take? Please give a brief answer using a single sentence and do not copy the steps.

This is a math question: [Question]. The following is information extracted from the question:
Information 0: [Information 0]
...
The following are the first a few steps in a solution to the problem:
Step 0: [Step 0]
...
Step i-1: [Step i-1]
Which previous steps or information does the next step [Step i] directly follow from?

We are in the process of solving a math problem. We have some information from the problem:
Information 0: [Information I0]
...
The following are some previous steps:
Step 0: [Step S0]
...
The target for the next step is:
[Target]
Please try to achieve the target with the information from the problem or previous steps.

The following are 2 solutions to a math problem.
Solution 1: [Regeneration output]
Solution 2: [Step i]
Compare the key points from both solutions step by step and then check whether Solution 1 'supports', 'contradicts' or 'is not directly related to' the conclusion in Solution 2. Pay special attention to the difference in numbers.

The following is a question and a solution to it from a student. Carefully check whether the solution is correct step by step. End your response with your conclusion that starts with "Correct", "Wrong" or "Not Sure".
Question: [Question]
Solution: [Step 0, Step 1,..., Step n]

The following is a question and the first a few steps in its solution.
Question: [Question]
Solution: [Step 0, Step 1,..., Step i-1]
Check the correctness of the next step: [Step i]
Please consider the information it relies on and check step by step. Please end your response with your conclusion that starts with "Correct", "Wrong" or "Not Sure".

Given the following information:
Information 0: [Information I0]
...
Step 0: [Step S0]
...
Check the correctness of the next step [Step i]
Please check for grounding errors, reasoning errors and calculation errors step by step. Please end your response with your conclusion that starts with "Correct", "Wrong" or "Not Sure".

Solve the following problem step by step. Please start each step with "Step :" and split sentences in each step with "\n\n". Please finish you response with "So the answer is ...".
Problem: [Question]

The following is the solution to a math question: Question: [Question] Solution: [steps] Are there variables in the solution? If so, please list the definition of variable in the form of "1. variable is defined as...".
Alice apples/oranges/bananas grounding, reasoning and calculation check exemplar from Ling et al. (2023)

results.claim: Directly asking the LLM to check an answer deems it correct more than 90% of the time regardless of truth; the claim is attributed to Ling et al. (2023), not measured here
results.source: Ling et al. 2023, Deductive verification of chain-of-thought reasoning
results.setup: Direct LLM self-checking of answers; finding of Ling et al. (2023) (Deductive Verification), cited in Section 3
results.note: The paper's own related observation: direct whole-chain prompting gives FP and TP both 100% on MATH and 98% on GSM8K 'as observed by Ling et al. (2023)'.
results.quote: with Ling et al. (2023) finding answers checked in this way are deemed correct more than 90% of the time regardless of whether they actually are

results.claim: Majority voting accuracy saturates with larger ensembles; SelfCheck keeps improving
results.setup: MathQA 100-question subset, GPT-3.5, up to 50 solutions per question (Fig 5). Majority voting never exceeds its n=9 accuracy, below what SelfCheck gets with the smaller ensemble.
results.quote: with the accuracy of majority voting never going above that achieved when n = 9

limits: Only math reasoning (GSM8K, MathQA, MATH); generality to other domains is asserted, not tested.
MATH evaluated on a subset (MATH*) from Ling et al., size not stated, due to limited resources.
GPT-4 experiments use only 500 questions per dataset and 2 solutions; GPT-4 checker gives -0.2±0.2 on GSM8K (no gain).
Ablations use only 100 MathQA questions, so verification accuracies (66.7 vs 55.0 etc.) carry large uncertainty; no error bars given.
No decoding settings (temperature, top_p, max tokens) are stated; closed OpenAI models of 2023, snapshots since retired.

Comparisons to DV and SV are against gaps quoted from other papers with different generators, so not directly comparable. The text names them inconsistently: Fig 2 caption says DV is Weng et al. (2022) and SV is Ling et al. (2023); Section 4 says SV is Ling et al. and DV is Weng et al.; the related-work section says SV is Weng and DV is Ling.
Cost of checking (multiple LLM calls per step) is not quantified.
Prompts were devised with a few MathQA training samples, so MathQA is not fully held out for prompt design.
